To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) score-based generative modeling (SGM) is a powerful framework that can be used to model data distributions in a wide variety of domains and (2) LSGM is a novel approach that enables training SGMs in the latent space of a VAE, which leads to faster sampling and better results in terms of FID and likelihood.

Score-based generative modeling in latent space (LSGM) achieves state-of-the- art results on several benchmark datasets, and that the key to the success of LSGM is a novel score matching objective, an improved score parameterization, and variance reduction techniques.

we introduce a novel score-based generative model (SGM), the latent score-based generative models, that is trained in a latent space and is more expressive, faster, and easier to train compared to the existing SGMs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of generating new samples of images from a given dataset.
the development of new machine learning techniques for generative modeling of data.
the problem of modeling the distribution of data in a way that allows us to generate new samples that are similar to the data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

LSGM is a novel and powerful generative modeling approach that outperforms previous methods in terms of sample quality, coverage, and sampling time, while being applicable to both continuous and discrete data.
LSGM is a novel approach that enables the application of SGMs in latent space, allowing to train more expressive models, sample faster and apply to non-continuous distributions.
LSGM achieves a new state-of-the-art in terms of FID on CIFAR10, while being on par in terms of sample quality with other SGMs on the more complex CelebA-HD256 dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel generative model that is based on the score matching framework.
LSGM is a novel approach that moves SGMs from data to latent spaces.
we propose a novel generative modeling approach, the latent score-based generative model, that trains a score-based generative models in a latent space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by moving generative models to the latent space, we can achieve more expressive and efficient generative models.
SGMs are a promising generative framework and that training SGMs in latent space is a promising direction to explore.
SGMs can be applied in a wide range of scenarios and benefit from the use of a latent space.
